accepted.sentence: In fanfare writing, its forceful attacks can announce arrivals or mark ceremonial moments with a projecting brass sound.
A rounded, sustained tone suits lyrical solos that draw on the broad, expressive phrasing of a human singing voice.
Historical reproductions help early-music groups recreate the brass sonorities associated with Renaissance and Baroque repertoire.
Some contemporary works ask players to sing while sounding notes, creating rough, beating textures for unusual musical effects.
Coordinated attacks across a section can give full-ensemble chords a sharply defined edge.
Low notes can underpin suspenseful film passages, adding weight beneath quieter orchestral textures.
In opera orchestras, sustained chords can reinforce dramatic scenes while careful balancing keeps the singers audible.
A low-register line can double the bass part, strengthening harmonic roots during full-ensemble passages.
